newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says will go to Helsinki summit as planned.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says will go to Helsinki summit as planned.

text.p: President Bill Clinton successfully underwent surgery for torn knee tendon on Friday and said he would go to Helsinki as planned for next week's summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
"I want you guys to quit giving my doctors a hard time about letting me go to Helsinki. We're all going to Helsinki. We have to go to Helsinki," Clinton said to reporters at Bethesda Naval Hospital.

Clinton spoke by audio feed to reporters gathered at the hospital just outside Washington as they listened to an account of the surgery by his doctors. His spokesman Mike McCurry said the surgical procedure, carried out without a general anaesthetic, lasted two hours and four minutes and was "successfully completed" at 4:43 p.m. (2143 GMT).

Dr David Adkison, head of orthopedic surgery at the hospital who led the team, said he saw no reason for Clinton to alter his plans to go to Helsinki. He is due to depart on Tuesday for the meetings with Yeltsin on Wednesday and Thursday.

"I think that he can travel," Adkison said, adding that Clinton would stay overnight in the hospital and may be able to go home on Sunday. "He tolerated the procedure very well and is very comfortable," Adkison said.
Clinton, 50, tore the tendon in his right knee when he slipped on stairs at the Florida home of Australian golfer Greg Norman early on Friday morning and was flown back for the emergency surgery.
